component.name: Day Planner
component.summary: Plan your day and track the time you spend on tasks

description.p: Day Planner is a light task list with time tracking for Phosh phones and the desktop. It keeps your tasks in the backup format of Super Productivity, so a backup moves between both apps without changes.

ul.li: Today's list, projects and tags
Tasks with subtasks, notes, estimates and a planned day
A timer per task that books the time on the day you worked
Repeating tasks, the same way as in Super Productivity
Habit journeys: small steps that grow, calm or with a game layer
Import and export of Super Productivity backups, and automatic backups
Works offline; needs no account and no network

description.p: Day Planner is an independent project and not affiliated with the Super Productivity project.

ul.li: Read sync folders that Super Productivity keeps compressed or encrypted; the encryption password stays in the keyring.

Journeys with the game now build something: the journey page shows one thing that is whole at every station and grows with the next (stepping stones become a bridge, a fireplace a house), with lanterns, pennants or flowers in front while a station is under way; you can change what is built and what hangs on it under "What you build".
A journey starts from a moment in your day, in your own words or at a fixed time; a journey you began earlier asks once whether its moment is yours.

Journeys offer everything QuestArc 4 does: stay at a station a while or pass one you already do, a gentle way back after a long break, letting a habit graduate and bringing it back, pairing a step with something you enjoy, an optional plan check, tying a new step to a habit, and QuestArc's texts in German.
Starting a journey lets you pick any start date and change what it builds, and a habit whose task no longer repeats can get a task again from the shelf.
The step you are growing shows on top of Today with what it builds; ticking its task lets a flower grow there, and the journey opens by itself only when a station is reached.
On wide windows the journey shows what it builds beside the station's card.

Choose what grows at a moment: under "Change this moment" you can pick another kind of thing (Home, Garden, Well or Lookout) for the place, also after it has grown; it keeps the version it has reached, and "Use the suggestion" brings back the journey's own.

Tap a place in the Valley to see its thing, the versions that stand and its routine in words; the pencil opens "Change this moment": its words, earlier or later in your day, the side of the path and its colour.
Read Super Productivity's Surgical sync folders too, with the latest changes applied.
Read the tasks Super Productivity keeps in its WebDAV, Nextcloud or local sync folder and import them, without changing the folder.
Tasks can remind you: set a reminder under a task's time, or a time and a reminder for a repeating task; the notification offers Done and Snooze and also comes while Day Planner is closed.
Journeys ask once whether a reminder would help for the first weeks of a step, and say when you may no longer need it.

Journeys open on the Valley: one path through your day with a place for every moment, the thing each routine builds, a lit lantern where a routine runs by itself, and the growing step as a card below.
The "What you build" page no longer offers a colour; a journey's colour now belongs to its place.
The thing a journey builds is marked by flowers that grow with each good day and open when the step is ready; "What hangs" is gone and the row of versions shows only what stands.
With a German system the journey pages are German throughout, including what a journey builds.
German umlauts in the journeys no longer turn into question marks when the system's language pack is missing.
Importing a backup that is older than the data on your device now warns how many tasks and journey entries would be lost, and keeps journey records made only on this device.
Journeys follow QuestArc 3.3: every journey shows what it builds, the stations are a list in the menu, and levels, XP, guardians and the choice between calm and game are gone.
Day Planner opens on your journeys once you have started one, and Journeys is the first entry of the sidebar.
A journey continued with a newer QuestArc is shown read-only instead of being changed, and journey data Day Planner does not understand is kept as it is.
Journeys: turn a habit into small steps that grow, with QuestArc's journeys, calm or with game, on the same data as Super Productivity's QuestArc plugin.
Tasks can repeat: every day, Monday to Friday, weekly, monthly, yearly or on a custom schedule, the same way as in Super Productivity.
Adding tasks, search, new lists, Mark as Done and the timer moved to the bottom of the screen, where the thumb reaches them.
Deleting a task or a list and finishing the day can be undone from the message that follows.
The app is now called Day Planner.
Choosing another project on a task's page no longer closes the app.
The journey no longer opens after every change in your lists; it comes forward only when you tick off its station's task.
Swiping from the left edge goes back again, from a task to its list and from a list to the lists.
On the phone, a swipe from a list goes back to the overview of lists, as in Ephyra.

description.p: First version: Today, projects and tags, tasks with subtasks and a timer, in Super Productivity's backup format.
